text:
For eight years, Rob Bilott's job was keeping chemical companies out of trouble.
Cincinnati lawyer. Corporate defence. He read their permits. He learned how disclosure worked and how it didn't. He was good at it.
October 1998. A phone call. Thick West Virginia accent. Wilbur Tennant, cattle farmer, Parkersburg. His cows were dying.
Rob nearly put the phone down. Then Tennant named the town. Rob's grandmother lived there. That is the only reason he listened.
Tennant drove to Cincinnati with 22 videotapes.
Dead cattle, filmed one at a time. Black teeth. Eyes turned blue. Foam at the mouth. Buzzards would not touch the bodies. On one tape Tennant cuts an animal open himself and holds the organs to the camera. Tumours everywhere.
His farm sat below a landfill. DuPont had bought that land from Tennant's own brother and promised it was just household waste.
A creek ran through it. The cattle drank from it. Tennant found a pipe pouring green liquid in and rocks bleached white around it.
Every lawyer in the county said no. Every vet said no. DuPont was the town's payroll.
Rob said yes.
DuPont sent its own vets. Their report landed in January 2000. No chemical problem. The farmer was simply bad at farming.
Wilbur Tennant had raised cattle his entire life. He buried 153 of them.
So Rob used the only weapon he had. Discovery. Every document DuPont held on that landfill.
Boxes came. Then more boxes. 110,000 pages, unsorted, out of order. He sat on his office floor for months and read all of it.
Then he found the name. PFOA. C8. Not on any regulated list. Not illegal. Which is exactly why it never appeared in a permit.
DuPont had used it to make Teflon since 1951. The waste went to the landfill. The landfill went to the creek. The creek went to the cattle.
And then he found the studies. DuPont's own.
1961. Fed to rats. Enlarged livers. They knew that year.
1984. They tested the town's drinking water and found their own chemical in it. Told nobody.
1985. They measured the creek the cattle drank from. A hundred times over their own internal safety limit. Told nobody.
Their doctors tracked their own staff. Cancers. Two of seven babies born to women in the Teflon unit had birth defects. Filed away.
Rob sat on that floor and understood it was never a cow case. Every tap in that town ran through it. Seventy thousand people.
March 2001. He wrote a 972-page letter to the federal government and handed over every secret document he had. Then he sued DuPont for the whole town.
The town hated him for it. His own partners asked him what he was doing.
2004. DuPont offered $70 million and water filters. He could have taken the money and gone home.
Instead he traded it. He convinced 69,000 residents to give blood and built the largest health study of its kind, funded by DuPont and beyond DuPont's reach.
2012. The panel reported. Six diseases linked, including kidney cancer, testicular cancer and thyroid disease.
Now there was nothing left to argue. Around 3,500 people sued. First trial, $1.6 million. Second, $5.6 million. Third, $12.5 million. February 2017, DuPont folded and paid $670.7 million.
It cost him his health. In 2010 his vision blurred and his speech slurred. Strokes, at 45. He kept working.
2019. He published Exposure. Hollywood arrived the same year. Mark Ruffalo played him in Dark Waters. Millions watched it, then went and checked their own water.
It is in rain now. In Antarctic ice. In polar bears. In almost every human being alive. It does not break down in water, in soil, or in you.
April 2024. The first federal drinking water limits in history.
Now think about what happened next.
May 18, 2026. The EPA proposed rescinding those limits for four of the six chemicals, and giving water systems until 2031 to meet the two that survive. The comment period closed in July.
Twenty years of work. Two years of law.
Rob Bilott is 61 and still at the same firm. In March this year an Ohio court let his new case move toward certifying a class of every resident with these chemicals in their blood. Eleven million people.
Wilbur Tennant never saw any of it. He died of cancer in 2009. Rob still keeps the videotapes.
There is a non-stick pan in your kitchen right now.
Go and read the label. It will tell you nothing.
That was always the point.

~Weird But True

text:
Oil just closed above $100 as the U.S.-Iran conflict tightened the Strait of Hormuz. Brent settled at $101.21.

Meta jumped more than 6% against a falling market as Muse AI usage blew past expectations.

And after the close, Navan raised guidance while AeroVironment posted record backlog and American Eagle fell after a tariff-refund-heavy earnings beat.

Everything that mattered in the market today:

👉 COMPANIES

1. $AAPL: Apple unveiled the $1,999 iPhone Duo, its first foldable iPhone, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max at John Ternus's first major product event as CEO.

2. $META: Meta said early usage of its Muse AI agent exceeded internal expectations; Muse can access other apps to handle tasks such as email, reservations, travel and payments.

3. $GOOGL: Google committed €13B ($15.1B) to Finnish AI infrastructure over 2027-2028 and signed a 22-year nuclear-power agreement covering up to 50% of Fortum's Loviisa plant capacity.

4. $CHYM: Chime agreed to acquire nationally chartered Stride Bank for $590M in cash, gaining a faster route to full-stack banking ownership and more than $100M of expected net synergies.

5. $LYFT: Lyft shares fell sharply as investors digested a CFO transition while the company reaffirmed its financial guidance.

6. $BURU: NUBURU said NYSE American trading is scheduled to resume September 14 under ticker BURU following its 1-for-40 reverse split.

7. $BCHT: Birchtech said it plans to begin repurchasing shares under its previously authorized $5M buyback program on or after September 14.

8. $IVDA: Nasdaq granted Iveda an additional 180 days, through March 1, 2027, to regain compliance with the $1 minimum-bid requirement.

9. $PHGE: BiomX's 1-for-10 reverse split became effective September 9, reducing outstanding shares from about 26.7M to about 2.7M.

10. $LFT: Lument Finance Trust's 1-for-10 reverse split becomes effective after the September 9 close, with split-adjusted NYSE trading beginning September 10.

11. F5/FFIV: F5 expanded its AI-security platform with Workforce AI Security as enterprises increase controls around employee use of generative AI.

12. $WDC: Western Digital closed higher despite the broad selloff as AI-storage demand and data-persistence economics remained in focus.

13. $FORTUM/GOOGL: Fortum said its Google nuclear PPA should lift group comparable return on net assets by roughly 1.4 percentage points once 50% of Loviisa output is contracted.

14. $MSTR: Strategy remained exposed to bitcoin weakness after recently reporting 845,050 BTC held at an average cost of $75,412.

👉 EARNINGS

15. $CHWY: Chewy reported Q2 net sales of $3.33B, up 7.3%, net income of $80.5M and adjusted EBITDA of $226.7M; adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 90 bps to 6.8%.

16. $SAIL: SailPoint reported fiscal Q2 revenue of $308.8M, up 17%, ARR of $1.231B, up 25%, and SaaS ARR of $847M, up 36%; 97% of net new ARR came from SaaS.

17. $BRZE: Braze reported Q2 revenue of $227.2M and adjusted EPS of $0.19, both above expectations, but weak Q3 EPS guidance drove a sharp selloff.

18. $INNV: InnovAge reported full-year revenue of $989.7M, up 15.9%, adjusted EBITDA of $94.6M, up roughly 175%, and a near-breakeven net loss of $0.7M.

👉 FDA / BIOTECH

57. ROIV: Roivant remained in focus after mosliciguat cut pulmonary vascular resistance by 56.3% versus placebo in Phase 2 pulmonary-hypertension data.

58. PHVS: Pharvaris remained supported by Phase 3 CHAPTER-3 data showing an 83% reduction in HAE attack rates versus placebo.

59. NVS: Novartis remained under pressure after sequential late-stage failures in myotonic dystrophy and Lp(a)-lowering cardiovascular outcomes.

60. AMGN: Amgen remained sensitive to Novartis' Lp(a) failure because of read-through risk to olpasiran.

61. DYN: Dyne remained exposed to negative DM1 read-through following Novartis' failed del-desiran study.

62. SRPT: Sarepta remained under pressure from broader RNA-based muscle-disease read-through concerns.

63. PEPG: PepGen also remained exposed to investor repricing of DM1 programs after the Novartis failure.

64. NAMS: NewAmsterdam Pharma remained a key cardiovascular biotech watch as investors reassess lipid-lowering targets after the pelacarsen failure.

👉 MANAGEMENT CHANGES

65. LYFT: Lyft's CFO transition weighed on shares even as management reiterated financial guidance.

66. AAPL: John Ternus led his first major Apple product launch as CEO, marking a high-profile test of the post-Tim Cook leadership transition.

👉 PRODUCT / PARTNERSHIPS

67. META: Muse offers free basic access plus paid subscription tiers and is designed to execute actions across email, calendar, payments, health, shopping and smart-home apps.

68. AAPL: The iPhone Duo features a 7.6-inch foldable display, Apple Pencil support and a $1,999 starting price; launch is scheduled for October 23.

69. GOOGL: Google's Finland plan includes three new data centers, new wind contracts, a 94-MW battery system and long-term nuclear power procurement.

70. FORTUM/GOOGL: The Fortum-Google deal begins at lower contracted volumes in 2028 and scales to as much as 50% of Loviisa output from 2030 through 2049.

71. F5/FFIV: F5 expanded AI security controls aimed at governing enterprise use of generative-AI tools.

72. NAVN: Navan introduced an OpenTable partnership to bring restaurant discovery and reservation booking into its AI travel assistant.

73. SAIL: SailPoint said AI-related solutions represented more than 30% of new ARR as it expands identity controls for human and agentic users.

👉 MARKET THEMES

74. SPY/QQQ/DIA: The S&P 500 fell 0.48% to 7,636.46, the Nasdaq dropped 0.64% to 26,253.34 and the Dow lost 0.77% to 52,381.02.

75. IWM: The Russell 2000 fell 1.3% to 2,921.23, underperforming large caps as higher yields and oil hit smaller companies harder.

76. XLE/USO: Energy was the only S&P 500 sector to gain as Brent settled at $101.21 and WTI at $96.05.

77. META: Meta gained about 6% as strong early adoption of Muse made it one of the session's standout mega-cap winners.

78. AAPL: Apple slipped about 0.3% despite launching its first foldable iPhone, suggesting the event was largely anticipated by the market.

79. GOOGL: Alphabet fell about 2.3% as investors weighed its $15.1B Finland infrastructure commitment against already-heavy AI capex.

80. XOM/CVX: Exxon Mobil and Chevron each rose more than 2% as oil moved above $100.

81. CASY: Casey's fell roughly 15.6%, ranking among the S&P 500's largest decliners.

82. DDOG: Datadog rose about 7%, one of the strongest S&P 500 gainers.

83. AKAM: Akamai gained more than 6% as select infrastructure software names outperformed.

84. WDC: Western Digital rose more than 3% while the broader market fell, extending AI-storage strength.

85. AMD: AMD gained about 3.6%, reinforcing relative strength in AI semiconductor exposure.

86. VRT: Vertiv fell about 7%, showing that AI-infrastructure names were not uniformly bid despite strong sector fundamentals.

87. CMCSA: Comcast fell about 6.7%, among the session's largest S&P 500 decliners.

88. CHTR: Charter Communications fell about 6.7%, extending pressure in cable and broadband equities.

89. KMB: Kimberly-Clark dropped about 4.8%, reflecting weakness in defensive consumer names.

90. BKNG: Booking Holdings fell about 4.4% as higher oil and travel-cost concerns weighed on travel-related stocks.

91. BRZE: Braze fell about 20% despite beating quarterly expectations as investors focused on weaker near-term EPS guidance and limited AI-driven top-line acceleration.

92. TTAN: ServiceTitan suffered a record selloff after investors focused on forward growth expectations despite improving margins and cash flow.

93. CHYM: Chime gained after the Stride deal initially pushed shares sharply higher, though gains moderated as investors digested execution and regulatory considerations.

94. TLT/IEF: The 10-year Treasury yield rose to about 4.85% after the Treasury's $6B buyback plan disappointed investors expecting a larger intervention.

95. FED: Higher oil and yields kept the possibility of a September Fed hike alive ahead of PPI and CPI.

96. VIX: Market breadth weakened sharply as geopolitical inflation risk and higher yields outweighed isolated AI winners.

97. BARCLAYS: Barclays raised its 2026 year-end S&P 500 target to 7,950 from 7,800 and lifted its 2026 EPS forecast to $365 from $337.

👉 STOCKS TO WATCH

98. ORCL: Oracle reports September 10 after the close; OCI growth, AI backlog conversion, capex intensity and financing remain the core variables.

99. ADBE: Adobe reports September 10 after the close, with AI monetization, ARR growth and leadership-transition execution in focus.

100. CPRT: Copart reports September 10 after the close, with salvage volumes, pricing and insurance-claims trends in focus.

101. KR: Kroger reports September 11, offering a read on grocery inflation, traffic and consumer trade-down behavior.

102. PPI: Thursday's U.S. producer-price report is the first major inflation test after oil crossed $100.

103. CPI: Friday's CPI report is the week's most important macro catalyst ahead of the September 15-16 Fed meeting.

104. AEO: American Eagle will be watched for follow-through after its revenue beat was overshadowed by below-consensus comparable sales and reliance on tariff refunds.

105. AVAV: AeroVironment will be watched after record backlog and a strong EPS beat, with investors assessing execution against $2.125B-$2.225B annual revenue guidance.

106. NAVN: Navan will be watched after raising annual revenue guidance and adding BoomPop, testing whether travel demand can stay resilient through higher fuel costs.

107. META: Meta's Muse rally puts monetization, retention and security execution under the microscope after early usage exceeded expectations.

108. AAPL: Apple's iPhone Duo launch shifts attention to preorders, ASP mix and whether a $1,999 foldable can materially lift hardware revenue.

109. GOOGL: Alphabet's Finland investment puts AI-capex returns and long-duration power contracting in focus.

👉 DEEP ANALYSIS / MARKET INTELLIGENCE

110. AI CAPEX / POWER: Google's €13B Finland buildout plus a 22-year nuclear PPA shows that AI infrastructure is increasingly constrained by electricity procurement, not just GPUs. The key read-through is that power contracts are becoming quasi-capacity reservations: Fortum expects the deal to lift group RONA by about 1.4 percentage points once 50% of Loviisa output is contracted. That creates a second-order opportunity set across utilities, nuclear operators, batteries and grid infrastructure.

111. OIL / RATES: Brent at $101.21 and the 10-year Treasury near 4.85% create a double discount-rate shock: energy raises headline inflation while higher yields compress equity multiples. This is particularly difficult for small caps, which fell 1.3%, and for leveraged consumer businesses. The market is now testing whether the Iran-driven oil shock is temporary or persistent enough to force the Fed tighter.

112. META VS APPLE: Meta gained about 6% on a software-first AI catalyst while Apple slipped despite unveiling its first foldable phone. This suggests investors currently value visible AI engagement and monetization optionality more than premium hardware novelty. Apple's $1,999 Duo may lift ASPs, but Meta's Muse can scale across an installed base without the same inventory and component-cost burden.

113. GOOGLE CAPEX QUALITY: Alphabet's $15.1B Finland investment is large enough to matter, but the economic structure is differentiated: cold climate lowers cooling costs, nuclear secures baseload power and a 94-MW battery adds flexibility. The key question is not simply capex size but whether these design choices lower lifetime compute cost enough to defend returns on invested capital as AI infrastructure spending rises.

114. GME EARNINGS QUALITY: GameStop's adjusted EPS beat came while revenue fell 18.7%. Collectibles now represent 45.1% of sales and grew 57%, but investment gains materially boosted reported profit. The key read-through is that core retail mix is improving even as total sales shrink; investors should separate recurring operating income from portfolio gains when valuing the business.

115. TTAN / SOFTWARE EXPECTATIONS: ServiceTitan's revenue grew 21%, operating margin improved to 15.2% and free cash flow reached $50.5M, yet the stock suffered a record selloff. This is a classic expectations problem: improving economics are insufficient when the market is pricing faster AI-led growth. The divergence shows how software valuation is migrating from “growth at any price” toward growth plus proof of AI monetization.

116. CHIME VERTICAL INTEGRATION: Chime's $590M Stride Bank acquisition targets more than $100M of net synergies, implying potential gross synergy value above 20% of the purchase price before discounting and integration costs. Bringing banking infrastructure in-house can lower sponsor-bank fees and funding costs, but it also moves Chime deeper into regulated balance-sheet risk. The acquisition changes the company from a fintech distribution model toward a more vertically integrated bank-tech hybrid.

117. NAVAN / BUSINESS TRAVEL: Navan's gross booking volume rose 45% while revenue grew 35%, and the company raised annual guidance despite geopolitical uncertainty and higher energy costs. This suggests corporate travel is currently benefiting from AI investment, conferences and dealmaking strongly enough to offset macro friction. If sustained, travel-tech demand could become a second-order beneficiary of the AI capex cycle rather than merely a consumer-spending proxy.

text:
Andrew Tulloch is leaving Meta today. Here's what you need to know.

Tulloch, a star AI researcher, is departing Meta less than a year after rejoining the company. He didn't say in his note to employees where he's headed next.

Meta reportedly offered him a pay package worth more than $1 billion over six years to lure him back, one of the highest-paid offers in tech history. He initially turned it down, then accepted two months later in October 2025.

Before rejoining Meta, Tulloch spent 11 years there, left in 2023 for OpenAI, then co-founded Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab. He reportedly delayed this latest exit until Meta shipped its new open-source Muse AI assistant.

Key numbers:
- $1 billion+: reported pay package to rejoin Meta
- 6 years: length of the compensation deal
- 11 years: Tulloch's earlier tenure at Meta before 2023
- <1 year: time back at Meta before this departure

Meta has not commented publicly on where Tulloch is headed next.

text:
A sudden and unexpected act of kindness can make anyone’s day. One Saturday afternoon, Officer Cameron Tucker and his wife, Justine, were eating an early dinner at the Zaxby’s restaurant in Deland... 

It was just a regular day and a regular dinner, until a young man approached the couple. 

That young man is named Juan, who is an African American college student. 

He asked the police officer if he could pray over him, to keep him protected. 

Cameron and his wife were surprised by this, but certainly accepting of the young man’s offer. 

With that, Juan put his hand on Cameron’s shoulder and prayed for his safety with his dangerous profession. 

Justine posted about it on social media, saying: “After crying my eyes out, we got to have an amazing conversation with this gentleman. 

He was on fire for God and you could feel His presence in the room. 

He said that he felt compelled to talk to us and to pray over Cameron.” 

Juan plays football at Stetson University in Deland, Florida and he’s a member of the Fellowship of Christian Athletes. 

When in high school, he graduated with honors. 

The photo taken of Juan praying over the officer was taken by Justine. 

Juan’s grandmother, Berta O’Neil, was extremely proud of her grandson for doing what he did in the photo. 

It showed just how powerful a young person’s actions can be. 

And ever since Juan prayed over Cameron, the two have kept in regular touch."

More of the background will I hope help you understand the power of the moral

September 21, 2019. Sergeant Cameron Tucker of the Volusia County Sheriff’s Office and his wife Justine were eating at Zaxby’s in DeLand, Florida, when 21-year-old Stetson University student Juan O’Neal approached their table and asked to pray for the deputy’s safety. Justine took the photo and posted it on Facebook; it quickly went viral. 
Juan O’Neal (sometimes spelled O’Neal) was a senior marketing major, football player, ROTC cadet, and member of the Fellowship of Christian Athletes. He is from the Columbus, Georgia area (Harris County High School, class of 2016) and the son of a law-enforcement officer; his father, Ron O’Neal, served with the Columbus Police Department and later as a Harris County deputy. Juan has said he felt compelled to pray because he understood the stress officers and their families face. He had already spoken with Tucker at the counter before coming over to the table

Ancient and Esoteric Secret Societies of Germania

Several historical and esoteric groups in German-speaking lands have claimed ancient or mythic roots, blending folklore, mysticism, and political agendas. While many were modern creations, they often invoked “ancient” or “Germanic” identities to lend legitimacy.
1. Germanenorden (Order of Teutons)
https://t.co/s8vl6aZwpm
Founded in 1911, this secret society claimed to preserve Germanic traditions and was linked to the Thule Society. It was part of a broader völkisch movement that sought to revive a mythical Germanic past
2. Thule Society (Thule-Gesellschaft)
https://t.co/nUU8sKIFYq
Established in Munich in 1918, the Thule Society began as a study group for Germanic antiquity but evolved into a far-right, occultist organization. It was closely tied to the Germanenorden and is historically notable for sponsoring the early Nazi Party
Fresh German Bread – One Stop German Shop
https://t.co/zj9hWfUmN0
Its ideology combined anti-communism, racial antisemitism, and a romanticized view of Germanic origins.
3. Vril Society
https://t.co/JJVX7C02ys
Though not exclusively German, the Vril Society was influenced by German occultists and was part of a broader European esoteric network. It promoted the idea of a “Vril” energy force and was associated with mystical and political conspiracies
4. Ordo Templi Orientis (O.T.O.)
https://t.co/mQRzeBOuSm
Founded in the early 20th century by Theodor Reuss, O.T.O. was an occult and magical order with roots in German-speaking Freemasonry. It combined Hermeticism, ceremonial magic, and esoteric philosophy, and was influential in European occult circles
5. Illuminati (Bavarian Illuminati)
https://t.co/Nxx5JHAHxi
Founded in 1776 in Bavaria, the Bavarian Illuminati was an Enlightenment-era secret society that opposed superstition and sought political reform. Though not “ancient” in origin, it became a symbol of hidden power and conspiracy
6. Rosicrucian and Sufi-Influenced Networks
https://t.co/hICqKS2H9S
https://t.co/hICqKS2H9S
Some figures, like Rudolf von Sebottendorff, were linked to Rosicrucian traditions and Sufi mysticism. These networks blended Eastern and Western esotericism, producing secret societies with quasi-religious and political aims
7. Asiatic Brethren and Other Esoteric Groups
https://t.co/3iEgei3S6I
The Asiatic Brethren and other obscure societies were part of a wider European occult scene, often claiming ancient wisdom traditions and using coded languages or symbols to conceal membership
Angel humans

Several historical and esoteric groups in German-speaking lands have claimed ancient or mythic roots, blending folklore, mysticism, and political agendas. While many were modern creations, they often invoked “ancient” or “Germanic” identities to lend legitimacy.
1. Germanenorden (Order of Teutons)
https://t.co/s8vl6aZwpm
Founded in 1911, this secret society claimed to preserve Germanic traditions and was linked to the Thule Society. It was part of a broader völkisch movement that sought to revive a mythical Germanic past
2. Thule Society (Thule-Gesellschaft)
https://t.co/nUU8sKIFYq
Established in Munich in 1918, the Thule Society began as a study group for Germanic antiquity but evolved into a far-right, occultist organization. It was closely tied to the Germanenorden and is historically notable for sponsoring the early Nazi Party
Fresh German Bread – One Stop German Shop
https://t.co/zj9hWfUmN0
Its ideology combined anti-communism, racial antisemitism, and a romanticized view of Germanic origins.
3. Vril Society
https://t.co/JJVX7C02ys
Though not exclusively German, the Vril Society was influenced by German occultists and was part of a broader European esoteric network. It promoted the idea of a “Vril” energy force and was associated with mystical and political conspiracies
4. Ordo Templi Orientis (O.T.O.)
https://t.co/mQRzeBOuSm
Founded in the early 20th century by Theodor Reuss, O.T.O. was an occult and magical order with roots in German-speaking Freemasonry. It combined Hermeticism, ceremonial magic, and esoteric philosophy, and was influential in European occult circles
5. Illuminati (Bavarian Illuminati)
https://t.co/Nxx5JHAHxi
Founded in 1776 in Bavaria, the Bavarian Illuminati was an Enlightenment-era secret society that opposed superstition and sought political reform. Though not “ancient” in origin, it became a symbol of hidden power and conspiracy
6. Rosicrucian and Sufi-Influenced Networks
https://t.co/hICqKS2H9S
https://t.co/hICqKS2H9S
Some figures, like Rudolf von Sebottendorff, were linked to Rosicrucian traditions and Sufi mysticism. These networks blended Eastern and Western esotericism, producing secret societies with quasi-religious and political aims
7. Asiatic Brethren and Other Esoteric Groups
https://t.co/3iEgei3S6I
The Asiatic Brethren and other obscure societies were part of a wider European occult scene, often claiming ancient wisdom traditions and using coded languages or symbols to conceal membership

1. He made the border a real border again. In a matter of months, Trump reduced illegal border crossings to their lowest level in half a century. Catch-and-release is finished. The wall is going up and even being expanded, “Remain in Mexico” is back, and the Administration reduced releases into the country by an incredible 99.9 percent.
2. He reversed mass migration. America recorded negative net migration in 2025 for the first time in at least half a century. So far, nearly 3 million illegal aliens have left the country, whether voluntarily or involuntarily: more than 675,000 forcibly deported and the rest “self-deported.” Many of those self-deportations were facilitated by the President’s innovative program to offer plane tickets and cash bonuses for illegals to leave, not only incentivizing good behavior but significantly reducing the cost of deportations. Citizenship and the law actually mean something again.
3. He signed the Laken Riley Act — and required detention of criminal illegal aliens. Named for an innocent girl murdered by an illegal alien, the Laken Riley Act requires federal authorities to detain illegals arrested for theft, burglary, shoplifting, assaulting police, or any crime causing death or serious injury. It also lets states sue officials who refuse to enforce it. Laken Riley should still be alive. This law will prevent tragedies like hers.
4. History’s biggest drop in violent crime, and the lowest violent crime rate in 126 years. According to FBI data, violent crime in America dropped an incredible 9.7 percent in 2025 — the largest one-year decline in history. Murder fell 18.1 percent, robbery fell 18.5 percent. And America’s violent crime rate is its lowest since 1900. This is what happens when you put the National Guard on the streets in crime-ridden blue cities: fewer victims, safer streets, and better futures for America’s poorest.
Trump Launched an American Industrial Supercycle
5. He made the 2017 tax cuts permanent…and better. The One Big Beautiful Bill locked in the largest tax cut in modern history, including the doubled standard deduction, the expanded Child Tax Credit, and 100 percent expensing for factories and equipment. It also delivered No Tax on Tips, No Tax on Overtime, an abolition of most taxes on Social Security benefits, and major relief for seniors. Every Democrat voted no. With the 2017 act set to expire in December 2025, that would have resulted in the largest tax hike in American history.
6. He repealed 129 regulations for every new one. In fiscal 2025, federal agencies finalized 646 deregulatory actions and just five regulatory actions: 129-to-1, and in nearly every case, the “one” was to repeal the others! OIRA says the savings exceeded those of Trump’s entire first term. That is more freedom, lower costs, and less bureaucratic sabotage. Of these, the crown jewel was the repeal of Obama’s 2009 “Endangerment Finding”, the legal foundation for the Green New Scam’s vehicle mandates. EPA calls it the largest deregulatory action in American history and estimates that by itself, it will save Americans more than $1.3 trillion. Trump also killed the federal EV mandate, restored Americans’ freedom to buy the cars and trucks they actually want, and even eliminated the incentives behind the almost universally hated start-stop button.
7. He secured $18 trillion in announced investment commitments. That’s nearly two-thirds the size of the entire American economy, building American factories, chip plants, data centers, energy projects, steel mills, shipyards, and supply chains employing American workers. Apple, Meta, NVIDIA, Micron, Hyundai, U.S. Steel, Ford, Taiwan Semiconductor, and many corporations and sovereign wealth funds are betting big on Trump’s America. No President has ever done anything remotely like it. And it’s just getting started.
8. He made “reshoring” and “reindustrialization” real, not a slogan. Ford is moving Lincoln production out of China. Toyota is shifting Tacoma production from Mexico to Texas. GM, Honda, Mercedes-Benz, Stellantis, and others are expanding U.S. production. The capital equipment pouring into the country is the machinery that’s building the growing boom.
9. He replaced lopsided trade deals with balanced, reciprocal trade. Trump used tariffs as leverage to reverse 80 years of lopsided trade deals that favored everyone but America, and to win new or improved agreements with trading partners accounting for more than half of global GDP. Those agreements open foreign markets, attack non-tariff barriers, defend strategic industries, and make it more profitable to build in America than to export American jobs.
10. He shifted global energy dominance from the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of America. Once the world’s largest energy importer — “exporting” $700 billion a year to our enemies — America now outproduces Saudi Arabia and Russia combined. The U.S. is also setting new records in oil, natural gas, and LNG exports, becoming the first country ever to export more than 100 million metric tons of LNG in a year. Trump also opened land, accelerated permits, expanded pipelines and export terminals, and made American energy a tool for prosperity and peace.
11. After four decades of nuclear paralysis, Trump brought five new reactors online in a single year. For more than 40 years, not one new privately developed non-light-water reactor reached criticality in America. Trump ordered at least three by July 4, 2026. DOE delivered four by the deadline, then a fifth just one month later. Decades of zero. One Trump summer: five. That is a genuine nuclear renaissance.
Trump Made Elections Matter Again
12. He broke the Deep State’s power to defy the elected branches. In Trump v. Slaughter, the Supreme Court ruled for the first time in 90 years that Article 2, Section 1 is still part of the Constitution: the President may fire subordinate officials in the executive branch, overturning the 1935 precedent that insulated “independent” agencies from voters’ control. Ever wonder why elections often seem to change nothing? How about one President and 5,000 political appointees vs. 2.8 million unfireable, unaccountable bureaucrats? THAT is the “Deep State”. Trump then made that victory real. For the first time in a century, all policy-making bureaucrats can now be fired for misconduct, incompetence, or defying lawful directives. The permanent bureaucracy no longer gets to veto the voters.
13. He ended nationwide injunction abuse. In Trump v. CASA, the Supreme Court sharply limited nationwide injunctions. A single, local, district judge should not be able to block a national policy for everyone, everywhere; and yet that’s exactly what they’ve done, nonstop, ever since Trump (and only Trump) took office in 2017. In restricting that unconstitutional power, the Court kneecapped the Black Robe Bureaucracy’s favorite tool of unlawful judicial supremacy.
14. He shut down USAID as a left-wing slush fund and shadow government. USAID had become a taxpayer-funded machine for exporting abortion, gender ideology, censorship, and left-wing politics. It had a bigger budget than the CIA and the State Department combined, absolutely no accountability whatsoever, and a penchant for overthrowing governments. Trump terminated it — completely — and moved real humanitarian aid under the State Department. Immediately, seven socialist Latin American governments lost re-election. Coincidence?
15. He shrank Federal employment to its lowest level in 60 years. From a high under Biden, the federal workforce is now its smallest since 1966. Workforce reductions, agency closures, and spending cancellations mean fewer bureaucrats paid to resist the voters. What’s more, when Biden left office, 94 percent of federal employees “worked” from home. The Trump administration cracked down: as Elon Musk put it, “you can work from the office or you can pretend to work somewhere else.”
16. He expelled DEI from the federal government. Trump eliminated federal DEI offices and barred race- and sex-based preferences across the executive branch. Government hiring and contracting are returning to merit and equality under the law, ending the grotesque Democrat idea that “fighting discrimination” requires the federal government to discriminate.
He Defended Faith and Family
17. He delivered sweeping pro-life reform. In his first term, Trump delivered the judges that overturned the abominable Roe v. Wade. Hardly anyone believed it could be done, or that Trump would do it. But he did, and a half-century nightmare finally ended. Since returning to office, Trump has enforced the Hyde Amendment prohibiting the use of federal funds to pay for abortions, reinstated and expanded the Mexico City Policy prohibiting federal funding of foreign abortions, ended federal fetal-tissue research, strengthened conscience protections, protected Medicaid from funding large abortion providers, and pardoned 23 pro-life activists prosecuted by Biden’s weaponized Justice Department. He’s also done everything within the Executive Branch’s power to defund Planned Parenthood. It would be nice if Congress did likewise. No President has ever done more to protect life. No one.
18. He got men out of women’s sports, and restored biological reality to federal policy. The United States government once again officially recognizes two sexes: male and female. Trump ended federal support for the chemical and surgical gender mutilation of children, stopped taxpayer funding of such irreversible abominations, and forced more than three dozen health systems to end or suspend their programs as well. Trump also enforced Title IX as written: women and girls deserve their own teams, trophies, scholarships, and locker rooms. The NCAA and other athletic organizations changed their rules in response. After years of Democrats doing everything they could to destroy women’s sports and ruin girls’ lives, Trump’s administration protects women and girls again.
19. He enacted America’s first nationwide school-choice program — and launched Trump Accounts. As part of the President’s One Big Beautiful Bill, Trump enacted America’s first-ever nationwide school choice program. The new Education Freedom Tax Credit helps fund scholarships for tuition, books, and other educational costs. That’s on top of the new Trump Accounts, which give every child a tax-advantaged stake in America’s future, including a $1,000 federal seed for eligible newborns. Parents gain power. Bureaucracies lose it. And children learn first-hand about free markets and future orientation.
20. He targeted anti-Christian bias and discrimination. Trump created the White House Faith Office, Religious Liberty Commission, and Task Force to Eradicate Anti-Christian Bias. He restored conscience protections and made clear that Christians do not surrender their First Amendment rights merely by entering public life.
He Restored Peace Through Strength and Put America First
21. He forced NATO to stop freeloading and increase defense spending by 250 percent. For decades, wealthy European governments underfunded their militaries, effectively sending America the bill and using American taxpayers to subsidize their bloated welfare states. Trump forced NATO to replace its old two-percent-of-GDP spending target with an enormous five percent by 2035. Allied spending is rising, American defense orders are soaring, and Europe is becoming a partner instead of a dependent.
22. He drove China out of the Caribbean. China spent years building strategic beachheads at both ends of the Panama Canal, in Cuba, and in Maduro’s Venezuela. Trump forced Panama out of Belt and Road, expanded American security access around the Canal, and captured Maduro, who now sits in a New York jail cell awaiting trial. Beijing’s planned encirclement of the United States collapsed. The Monroe Doctrine is back. Call it the Donroe Doctrine.
23. He brokered eight peace deals in just eight months. In eight months, Trump brokered peace in eight conflicts spanning four continents, including wars that had gone on for as much as 40 years. It’s a record unmatched by any other President.
24. He launched and funded Golden Dome, the first-ever true missile defense for the U.S. population. Ronald Reagan dreamed of making nuclear missiles obsolete through his Strategic Defense Initiative. Today, Trump is actually building it: a layered homeland shield with space-based sensors and interceptors, conventional defenses, and new technologies including microwave systems to destroy drone swarms and directed-energy weapons (yes, lasers) that can replace an $11 million missile with $2 of electricity. Congress has funded the initial $25 billion, with far more on the way once it passes the NDAA this fall. Better a shield than a sword.
25. He restored the warrior ethos — and reversed the recruiting crisis. After years of missed targets under Biden, every active military component met or exceeded its 2025 recruiting goal. Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth refocused the newly renamed Department of War on actually winning wars, while pouring resources into shipbuilding, munitions, drones, missile defense, and America’s atrophied industrial base. Young Americans once again believe their Commander-in-Chief is worth serving. And they’re showing up en masse.

【日刊 アジアのエネルギー最前線】中国の専門家ら，ネパールで発生した洪水と気候変動との関連性を指摘，厳しい監視下に置かれる

（写真地図など末尾）

中国の専門家らは、チベット・ネパールで発生した死者を出した洪水と気候変動との関連性を指摘。水力発電プロジェクトは厳しい監視下に置かれる，との趣旨である。特に中国が目指すブラマプトラ川の屈曲点を利用する Medog Project に焦点が当たる。ここはネパールの渓谷よりも更に地形は厳しい。ただ，氷河湖決壊という危険因子ではなく，恐らく収縮により生じた岩盤の裂け目からの影響が大きい。いずれにしても，中国政府が，これまでの開発スピードを落としてくることが予想される。

◆260910 Chinese experts link deadly Tibet-Nepal flood to climate change; hydropower projects face scrutiny   Greater Kashmir https://t.co/adFhvjSvvs
The massive flash flood that struck the Tibet-Nepal border on August 26 has put China's numerous hydropower projects in the region, including the ...

（記事概要）

この記事は、中国の巨大インフラ開発、とりわけチベットのヤルンツァンポ川下流に計画されるMedog（墨脱）水力発電計画を、最近のヒマラヤ地域の大災害と関連づけて、その安全性や開発思想を問い直す内容です。

記事はまず、中国国内の巨大プロジェクトについて外部から得られる情報が限られている中、中国人起業家Joe Zhang氏がLinkedInに投稿した「China Breaks Ground On Massive Medog Hydropower Station」という文章を取り上げています。Zhang氏は、2025年7月19日にMedog Hydropower Stationの建設開始という「歴史的瞬間」を目撃したと述べています。

Medog計画は、チベットを流れるYarlung Zangbo（Yarlung Tsangpo、雅魯蔵布江）がインドに入ってBrahmaputra川となる直前の下流域に位置する巨大水力開発です。このため、中国国内だけの問題ではなく、下流国であるインドにとっても水資源、安全保障、環境などの面で大きな関心事となっています。

記事によれば、総投資額は1兆2,000億元、約1,700億ドルを超え、設備容量は7,000万～8,100万kW、すなわち70～81GWに達するとされています。規模のイメージとして、三峡発電所約3基分、あるいは白鶴灘発電所約5基分に相当する、世界でも例のない巨大水力開発として紹介されています。

Zhang氏はこの計画について、中国のインフラ建設能力を象徴するものであり、「国家の意志によって自然を進歩のために形作ることができる」ことを示すものだという趣旨の評価をしています。しかし記事は、この「自然を形作る」という発想を、最近ネパールと中国側チベットを襲った大規模な氷河・洪水災害の後では、以前と同じようには受け取れないと指摘しています。

ヒマラヤでは、氷河、急峻な峡谷、地滑り、地震などの自然条件そのものが非常に大きなリスクを持っています。そこへ道路、ダム、トンネル、行政施設、レーダーなどの巨大インフラが急速に建設されれば、災害が発生した際の被害規模や連鎖的影響がさらに大きくなる可能性があります。

記事は、中国がチベットやネパール周辺で巨額のインフラ投資を進めてきたことについて、地域開発を促進しているという中国側の説明がある一方、戦略的な影響力拡大、いわゆる「開発の武器化」ではないかという懸念も存在するとしています。

そして今回のヒマラヤの災害を踏まえれば、中国自身も、巨大インフラを次々に建設する現在の開発方式が、地質的・気候的に極めて厳しいヒマラヤ地域で本当に持続可能なのかを問い直す必要がある、というのが記事の中心的な主張です。

特にMedog計画について重要なのは、単に「70～81GWという世界最大級の発電所」という問題ではなく、チベット高原 → Yarlung Tsangpo → Great Bend（大屈曲部）→ Medog巨大水力群 → インド国境 → Siang → Brahmaputra，という一つの巨大な河川・地質システムの中で考える必要があるという点です。

今回の記事は、私たちが先ほどネパールについて描いた、
**「One River, One Risk System」**
という考え方を、そのままYarlung Tsangpo–Brahmaputraにも当てはめる材料になっています。

鳥瞰図に発展させるなら、**Medogの巨大水力群だけを描くのではなく、Great Bendの約2,000m級の急激な落差、深い峡谷、氷河・地滑り・地震リスク、計画される水力カスケード、インド国境、Siang川、そして下流のArunachal Pradeshまでを一枚につなぐ**と、非常に意味のある図になると思います。

題名は例えば、**「Medog Hydropower Project ― Great Bendの巨大水力開発とヒマラヤ複合災害リスク」**とすると、今回のネパール鳥瞰図と対になる一枚になりそうです。
